title: Baby Birds with Mohawks Win Big Photo Prize!
summary: Have you ever seen a bird with a mohawk? Meet the punk rockers of the bird world! Three baby egrets, with spiky feathers sticking straight up, just won the top prize in Smithsonian Magazine's big photo contest. The photographer, Jacqueline Burke, calls them "The Punk Rockers" because they look like a tiny rock band. She spotted them at a rookery (a bird breeding ground) in New Jersey. The chicks were squabbling and pecking at each other, full of attitude. "Their little necks and heads were writhing," Burke said. "One would peck. The other would peck back." In the winning photo, the fluffy chicks are in front, but look closely—their parent's huge, gnarly feet tower behind them! The contest had over 17,000 photos from 108 countries. Other winners include a glowing chameleon, a boy cleaning a bull's horns in South Sudan, and a Navajo girl's coming-of-age ceremony with her horse. Burke, who is a 64-year-old veterinarian, only started photography in 2014. She traded her binoculars for a camera because she loves animals. "We need to save species like this and save moments like this," she says. These egret chicks were no bigger than golf balls when curled up. Now their punk-rock portrait is famous!
why_it_matters: This funny photo might make you smile, but it also reminds us that nature is full of incredible, real-life characters worth protecting—maybe your own backyard has a surprise too.

background_read: Egrets are graceful white herons that grow long, fluffy feathers during breeding season to attract mates—sometimes those baby feathers stand up in funny ways.
The Smithsonian Institution is a group of museums and research centers in the U.S., and its magazine holds a famous photo contest every year with entries from all over the world.
Jacqueline Burke was an animal doctor who started taking pictures in 2014; nature photography helps scientists and the public care more about protecting wild animals.
Article_Structure: WHO: Jacqueline Burke, a 64-year-old veterinarian turned photographer.
WHAT: Her photo of baby egrets with mohawk-like feathers won the top prize in Smithsonian Magazine's contest.
WHERE: The photo was taken at a rookery—a bird nesting site—in New Jersey.
WHY: The chicks' spiky looks and feisty behavior created a hilarious, unforgettable image that stood out among thousands of entries.

perspectives.description: The photo celebrates the wild, untidy beauty of baby birds and encourages people to notice and care about local birdlife.
Some might say a funny picture is not as 'serious' as wildlife photos showing danger or survival, but humor can make people remember conservation.
Burke started photography later in life with just a passion for animals—winning shows that anyone can turn a hobby into recognition.
